acceptance.output_evidence: (1) WHAT A REAL VENDOR PDF CARRIES THAT THE CENSUS-GENERATED SYNTHETIC CANNOT, AND WHICH CERTIFICATION ARM BREAKS FIRST. The criterion names four candidates -- fonts, ligatures, rotated tables, footnote markers. Three retained vendor PDFs were available to this cell, so these are MEASURED rather than guessed, and the answer to 'which breaks first' is not the one the list suggests. (i) FONTS AND LIGATURES -- MEASURED, AND IT IS ALREADY HAPPENING. Every page of all three vendor specimens carries the literal text '(cid:45)' where the 'fi' ligature belongs: '(cid:45)nancial instrument', in the footer disclaimer, 23 of 23 pages in overview, 31 of 31 in comparison, 35 of 35 in multicomp. THE SHARP PART: the same glyph is (cid:45) in two documents and (cid:46) in the third -- one vendor, one run, one day, a different font subset. A cid code is a per-document subset index, so ANY repair that maps a cid number to a letter is a guess about one file that is silently wrong on the next. The synthetic specimens produce ZERO cid occurrences, because PyMuPDF writes base-14 helv with no subsetting -- so this entire class is invisible to every synthetic-only arm. Row IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S10. WHICH ARM BREAKS FIRST: NOT a numeric certification arm. The damage lands in DISCLOSURE TEXT, which this cell emits into AnalysisReport.disclosures and which no arm certifies against coordinates at all -- disclosures carry a source_page and no bbox, by the contract's own shape. So the first thing to break is the one thing NOT being graded, and it breaks silently: '(cid:45)nancial' would reach a client-facing artifact through IB-s-14's export bundle with every numeric arm still reading N of N. This cell substitutes a visible '[?]' marker rather than healing the text, which converts a silent corruption into a visible one, and that is a mitigation rather than a fix. (ii) ROTATED TABLES -- NOT PRESENT in any of the three specimens and therefore UNTESTED, which I am naming rather than reporting as absent-by-inspection. pdfplumber's extract_words returns a bbox in page space with no rotation, so a rotated table's words would carry boxes whose top/bottom no longer correspond to reading order. The arm that would break is (b)'s L2 leg: the label neighbourhood is defined as the value's own TEXT ROW, and 'row' in a rotated region is a column. It would fail LABEL_NOT_IN_NEIGHBOURHOOD -- which is the SAFE direction (a refusal, not a wrong number) and is worth stating as the designed behaviour rather than as a success. (iii) FOOTNOTE MARKERS -- the dangerous one, and it is the answer to 'which breaks first' among the arms that actually grade numbers. A superscript marker adjacent to a value ('2.48 (1)') either merges into the token, in which case NUM_RE refuses it and the field goes UNLOCATED (safe), or splits into its own word, in which case it becomes a CANDIDATE NUMBER on the value's own row. The nearest-number rule would then be choosing between the value and its footnote index, and a marker printed to the LEFT of the value in a right-aligned column would win. That failure CERTIFIES: the marker's digit really is at those coordinates, its label really is on its row, and its unit really is the census's. L1, L2 and L3 all pass on a number that is not the measurement. None of the three specimens carries a footnote marker next to a value, so this is reasoned from the rules, not observed -- and it is the case I would put in front of a real-client specimen first. (iv) A FOURTH THE CRITERION DOES NOT NAME, AND IT ALREADY BIT. Values printed across a column boundary. A list-valued field rendered as a long string overlapped the next column and the extractor took FRAGMENTS of the overlapping glyph runs ('8,', '6,') as values -- which CERTIFIED, for the same reason a footnote marker would. It was found not by certification but by a mutant probe's false positives. The remedy was to refuse to ask (list and table units emit no scalar), because no amount of checking after the fact can catch a fragment that really is printed where the row says it is. (2) IS THE PAGE-COORDINATE GRAIN FINE ENOUGH TO CATCH A TRANSPOSED DIGIT? YES for the case the question means, NO for a case it does not, and the difference is worth the CVO's attention. The recorded bbox is the WORD box -- e.g. [300.0, 114.86, 325.51, 123.86], about 25pt wide and 9pt tall for a 5-character value -- so it is finer than the value itself, not merely finer than the line. A transposed digit (2.48 recorded where the page prints 2.84) is caught, and caught by TEXT comparison rather than by geometry: certification crops that box, reads '2.84', and no accepted rendering of 2.48 appears in it. The difference control demonstrates exactly this at 0.3 -> 1.3 and prints the six accepted renderings it rejected. THE CASE IT DOES NOT CATCH is a transposition in the SOURCE: if the vendor itself printed 2.84 where it meant 2.48, Opal's record ties perfectly to the vendor's document and certification says so, correctly. Certification is a claim about fidelity of transcription, never about the vendor's arithmetic, and the word 'certified' in a client-facing context could easily be read as the stronger claim. That is the sentence I would most want the CVO to weigh. A THIRD CASE sits between them: two DIFFERENT fields whose values happen to be digit-transpositions of each other, where the wrong one is located. The bbox grain does not help -- both are real numbers at real coordinates -- and what catches it is the L2 label tie, which is why that leg exists and why it has its own mutant (M2) and its own control. (3) THE STANDING GAP, restated because it bounds everything above. The vendor specimens are real YCharts output on SYNTHETIC HOLDINGS -- two positions, SPY $60,000 and AGG $40,000. A representative REAL-CLIENT specimen has dozens of positions, long wrapped names, per-cell as-of dates and pagination this extractor has never seen. That gap is the PRD's own, named on FWD-4 and FWD-8, and nothing here closes it.

mutant.description: FOUR mutants by monkeypatch, editing no production file. The risk is specific and not hypothetical here: an extractor and its certifier written by the same author in the same hour, against specimens that author also generated, can agree with each other for the wrong reason. M1 makes certification ignore the VALUE (the accepted-rendering set becomes the original token unconditionally, which is exactly what a careless 'compare against what we extracted' does). M2 makes it ignore the LABEL, against the leg value-at-coordinates cannot reach. M3 gives a chart-only region a number, against 'no number from a visual guess'. M4 removes the date-line exclusion, against arm (a).
mutant.expected: M1: the perturbed value stops reading VALUE_NOT_AT_COORDINATES. M2: the transposed label stops reading LABEL_NOT_IN_NEIGHBOURHOOD. M3: the chart census moves 0 -> 1 emitted and the row grades CHART_REGION_EMITTED_A_VALUE. M4: values taken from a date line move 0 -> non-zero. Each must make the arm's own predicate FALSE.
mutant.observed: mutants_fired_as_expected: true. M1 baseline VALUE_NOT_AT_COORDINATES -> mutant CERTIFIED (predicate false). M2 baseline LABEL_NOT_IN_NEIGHBOURHOOD -> mutant CERTIFIED (predicate false). M3 baseline 0 numeric values across 10 chart regions with all certified -> mutant 1 emitted and {CERTIFIED: 9, CHART_REGION_EMITTED_A_VALUE: 1} (predicate false). M4 baseline 47 located with 0 values from a date line -> mutant 64 located with 17 from a date line, 63 of 64 CERTIFIED (predicate false) -- the extractor harvesting 'Periodic Return - Total' = 8.0 from the token '8,' and 2026.0 from '2026', both off the 'Data as of:' line. M4 IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL: before the rule existed the extractor located 42 values per variant instead of 26 and the extra sixteen all CERTIFIED, because a date line's digits sit exactly where the extractor said they did -- a control that only mutated the CERTIFIER would never have found it. TWO DEFECTS IN THE CONTROLS THEMSELVES ARE RECORDED, because they are the more instructive half: (i) the M4 probe called extract._date_line_tops() at probe time -- the EXACT function M4 patches out -- so it went blind in the one run it existed to measure and reported a clean 0 on a mutant that had just harvested 17 extra values; the reference set is now captured from the unmutated module at import time. (ii) the first M4 probe detected dates by TOKEN SHAPE (ends in a comma) and returned 4 FALSE POSITIVES on the baseline, which turned out to be a SECOND, DIFFERENT real defect -- fragments of a list value rendered across a column boundary, now refused by NON_SCALAR_UNITS -- hiding behind noise attributed to the first. A probe whose positives you have to explain away is not measuring the thing it names. A FIFTH CONTROL SHIPS INSIDE THE BATTERY: arm (c)'s transposed-label control, and arm (amend)'s live probe that _keys still accepts a client name (arm (amend) FAILS if that gap ever stops being real, so this cell's guard cannot quietly become decorative). FULL OUTPUT: org/missions/D9/IRPT/IRPT_BCKEND/deliverables/0.9.0_WK_IRPT_BCKEND~3/IB-s-10_mutant_control_output.json
